stance.label: Taiwan bear-market bounce · DCA on plan

headline: Taiwan gains 3,274 points on the week, TSMC closes at its 2,180 high; foreigners sell 10th day
summary: Taiwan staged a strong bear-market bounce this week with TSMC taking the lead, but foreigners sold stocks for a 10th day and their net futures short hit a record; by the rules it is still a bear market with rising risk. The TAIEX is still below the −20% line at 39,858. US markets close early tonight on thin volume; next week, watch whether foreigners stop selling and the 12/4 payrolls.

watch.label: TAIEX bear line (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 39,308.08 on 11/27, about 1.4% below; retake it and hold the 200-day line 5 days to return to a pullback

watch.label: TAIEX 200-day line
watch.note: 5.7% below on 11/27, 10 days running; the line still rises (+2.47%); flattening would mean the long-term trend turns down

watch.label: QQQ tier 4 (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 633.93 on 11/25, 4.1% away; US closes early tonight, still the nearest tier of the nine

overview.lead: Taiwan's bounce passed to TSMC today, but foreigners are still selling and still adding futures shorts; this is a bounce inside a bear market.
points: The TAIEX closed at 39,308, up 9% on the week.
TSMC (2330) closed at its 2,180 high, adding about 262 points to the index.
Foreigners sold NT$29.6B, a 10th straight day, the smallest in several days.
Foreign net TAIEX futures short reached 107,503 contracts, a record for a third day.
US markets close early tonight; US figures stay at 11/25.

focus.lead: Both Taiwan funds' 11/26 NAVs recovered sharply while 0050 slipped today; the nearest tier is still QQQ.
points: Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV rose 5.68% on 11/26, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) 5.6%.
Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050) fell 0.48% today; TSMC rose but MediaTek (2454) closed lower.
0050 is −20.7% from its peak, 11.7% from tier 5.
QQQ is 4.1% from tier 4; US volume is thin tonight.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan Japan (TW000T5011A9) and the two AllianceBernstein funds have NAVs only to 11/25.

position.lead: No new trigger under the framework today; the nearest of the nine is still QQQ tier 4.
points: QQQ has used 45% of reserved cash; tier 4 is 4.1% away.
SPY has used 25% of reserved cash; tier 3 is 7.6% away.
0050 has used 70% of reserved cash; tier 5 is 11.7% away.
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 10.6% from tier 5 (11/26 NAV).
Neuberger Berman Taiwan Japan is 9.6% from tier 5 (11/25 NAV).
AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) is 8.0% from tier 3 (11/25 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology (LU0060230025) have used all tiers.

macro.lead: No more US data this week; rate-hike expectations still weigh on richly valued stocks, but credit markets are fine.
points: Core PCE rose 3.3% year on year (released 11/25); a December hike is nearly certain.
The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.85% (11/25).
High-yield spread is 3.72% (11/24), far from the 5% alarm line.
USD/TWD is 33.189 (11/26); the Taiwan dollar is weak but not plunging.

sentiment.lead: The index bounced for a week but breadth barely improved; the rally is concentrated in a few heavyweights.
points: Only 13% of Taiwan stocks are above their 200-day line; the breadth-collapse light stays on.
Only 8% are above the 50-day line, with 15 new lows.
CNN Fear & Greed is at 15, still extreme fear in US stocks.
VIX is 26.8 (11/26), down from the prior day.

sectors.lead: Heavyweights held up the market today while yesterday's electronic small caps gave back gains; rotation is fast.
points: Optoelectronics fell 2.17%; yesterday's leaders took a break.
Networking fell 1.39%, with Accton (2345) down 4%.
Building and construction rose 1.39%, among today's best sectors.
Electronic components are still down 29% over a month, the deepest drop.

taiwan.lead: Flows have not stabilized, but foreign selling is shrinking: a 10th straight day of selling at the lowest amount in days, while futures shorts keep growing.
points: Foreigners sold NT$29.6B; the 10-day streak totals about NT$500.5B.
Investment trusts bought NT$8.5B, a 3rd straight day; the three institutions sold NT$21.3B net.
Foreign net TAIEX futures short reached 107,503 contracts, a record for a third day.
Margin debt is NT$434.5B (11/26), down about a third in 20 days; deleveraging is deep.
Foreigners' top sells were financials such as SinoPac, First Financial and Mega.

watch.lead: US trades only half a day tonight; the real test is next week: when foreigners stop selling, and December payrolls, FOMC and CPI.
points: 11/27 US early close (Taipei 11/28 02:00), thin volume and no major data.
12/1 Jensen Huang faces a closed-door US House committee hearing.
12/4 US November payrolls (Taipei 21:30).
12/10 early morning FOMC decision; November CPI that evening.

regime.lead: By the rules Taiwan is still a bear market with rising risk; a big weekly rally is not enough to change the call. US stocks are still in a pullback.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 5.7% below its 200-day line, 10 days running, but the line still rises.
Systemic lights: 2 on for Taiwan, US below its 200-day line and Taiwan breadth collapse.
Credit, the economy and financial conditions are fine; high-yield spread is 3.72%, far from 5%.
Capitulation signals: 2 on, margin deleveraging and breadth washout; oversold and extreme foreign selling are not on.
Drops this deep have always gone past 20%: all 10 episodes since 2000, and 4 past 30%.
Of the 4 equally fast episodes only 1 went past 30%; the sample is too small, for reference only.
Flip condition: close back above 39,858, then hold the 200-day line at 41,699 for five days to return to a pullback.
Three or more risk lights would change the call to a bear driven by the economy or credit.
